chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The fasting person can submerge his body in water, pour water over his head, cool himself with his garment, cool himself with a hand-fan, and cool himself with a blower placed beneath him, but he must not immerse his head in the water.
ai.seo_question: Can a fasting person immerse their head in water to cool down?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the practical methods for a fasting person to alleviate heat, such as pouring water on the head and using fans, while explicitly prohibiting the full immersion of the head. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of avoiding *shubha* (doubtful acts) that might lead to accidentally swallowing water, thereby preserving the validity of the fast. It highlights the balance between physical comfort and ritual precision in daily Islamic practice.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Fasting one can stay still in the water and he can pour water upon his head, and he can cool himself with the (wet) clothes, and he can sprinkle (cool himself) with the ventilator, and he can sprinkle (cool himself) with the blower beneath him, but he cannot immerse his head into the water (to cool himself)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from fro al- ‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A person fasting can stay in water, pour water on one’s head or cool off with wet cloths, place wet comforting or a wet rug underneath, but must not immerse one’s head in water.’”
